outcome: Respiratory composite outcome (including meconium aspiration syndrome, neonatal bronchopulmonary disorders, neonatal transient tachypnea, and other neonatal respiratory distress requiring NICU admission)
cohort: 6,047 individuals with singleton gestations at 35 or more weeks who attempted labor and delivered at an academic hospital between June 1, 2015, and February 28, 2020.
finding: Intrapartum inhaled nitrous oxide use, compared to no analgesia, was associated with a decreased risk for NICU admission but an increased risk for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, while other neonatal outcomes did not differ.
